::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 20, 1897.  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown.  Printed in Coleridge, [<i>Life</i>](other_books/otherbook_40.qmd), 329.
:::

My dearest [Marianne](people/person_1546.qmd)-
[Raby](people/person_1221.qmd) will have told you that [my dear home companion](people/person_1462.qmd)'s long patience has ended.

She was really dying ever since last evening, though the end did not come till one o'clock to-day, holding my hand, and asking [Henry](people/person_184.qmd)'s prayers all the time till consciousness was gone, not many minutes before the end. I do not think in the relief I feel the difference it will make to me.

Your strawberries were really welcome to me---one of the few things she could take.-

Your most affectionate
C. M. YONGE.
